ben_infra: same pattern on 3 different nodes (ip-10-0-45-12, ip-10-0-47-03, ip-10-0-48-56). Node metrics show intermittent CUDA driver resets and a 20% spike in memory dirty pages right before crash. Could be a kernel/path that trips under quantized workload.

dave_sre: quick mitigation options: 1) route traffic off rtm-cc-12 -> fallback model variant, 2) set env to disable fused kernel, rollout restart, 3) cordon nodes with OOM spikes to avoid cascading. Recommend (1) + (2) immediate.

carol_engine: agreed. We pushed a change that enables an optimized fused kernel by default in the latest canary; if the fallback code path is the older non-fused kernel it should be safer. To flip quickly: set env var REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNEL=true on the deployment to force the older execution path. That avoids needing a rebuild.

alice (oncall): applying env change to deploy to fallback path and restarting pods now
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/rtm-cc REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNEL=true
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/rtm-cc
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/rtm-cc --watch
```

alice (oncall): routing change in progress to steer incoming traffic to rtm-cc-legacy variant while we stabilize. Updating envoy route weight: canary -> legacy 100%.
